data.body_html:
Marbella’s coastline offers two outstanding snorkeling destinations reachable only by boat: Cabopino to the east and Estepona to the west. Both are accessible from Puerto Banús in under 35 minutes, but they differ in depth, marine life, and water clarity. This guide compares Cabopino vs Estepona for your next Marbella boat rental snorkeling spots adventure, with real distances, depths, and practical advice for choosing the right charter.

Cabopino: Sandy Shallows and Seagrass Meadows

Cabopino lies 5 nautical miles east of Puerto Banús — a 15–20 minute cruise at 20 knots. The snorkeling area centres on the rocky headlands at the eastern end of Cabopino beach. Water depth ranges from 3 to 8 metres, with a sandy seabed interspersed with Posidonia oceanica seagrass meadows. These meadows are a protected habitat, so anchoring is only allowed in designated sandy patches. Visibility is typically 10–15 metres, best in the morning before the wind picks up.

Marine life here includes small bream, wrasse, and the occasional cuttlefish. The shallow depth makes Cabopino ideal for beginners or families with children. There are no entry fees, and you can anchor close to the shore. Our Astondoa 40 (12.5 m, 9 pax) or Azimut 39 (12.5 m, 11 pax) are perfect for small groups — both Tier A boats at €749/2h or €2,299/8h, including skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, and VAT.

Estepona: Rocky Reefs and Deeper Drops

Estepona is 10 nautical miles west of Puerto Banús — a 30–35 minute run. The snorkeling site is a rocky reef system off the Punta de la Doncella headland, with depths of 8–12 metres. The rocky bottom attracts more diverse marine life: octopus, moray eels, starfish, sea urchins, and larger bream. Visibility often reaches 15–20 metres on calm days, especially in late spring and early autumn.

Estepona is better suited to confident swimmers because of the deeper water and occasional swell. The reef has no designated anchoring zones, but your skipper will find a sandy patch nearby. For this trip, consider the Mangusta 80 (24 m, 12 pax) at €4,719 for a minimum 4 hours — includes a free jet ski for extra fun between snorkel sessions. All our boats have a swim platform and ladder for easy water access.

How to Choose Your Charter

Your choice of boat affects the snorkeling experience. For a half-day (4 hours) you can comfortably visit one spot. For a full day (8 hours), you could combine both — start at Cabopino in the morning, then cruise west to Estepona after lunch. The Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6 m, 12 pax) offers a spacious flybridge for sunbathing between swims. If you want speed, the Pershing 46 (14 m, 10 pax) cruises at 30+ knots, cutting travel time.

All charters include a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). For pricing on boats other than Tier A and Tier B, message us on WhatsApp. We’ll confirm availability and tailor the trip to your group.

What to Bring and Expect

  • Sun protection: SPF 50+, UV-protective rash guard, hat, sunglasses.
  • Towels and a change of clothes.
  • Underwater camera or GoPro — the clarity at Estepona is worth capturing.
  • Snorkel mask and fins (optional — we can arrange rental).
  • Seasickness tablets if you’re prone; the sea is usually calmest before 1 pm.

Water temperature in summer reaches 24–26 °C, so a thin wetsuit is optional. In May and October, expect 18–20 °C — a 3 mm shorty is comfortable.
